---
title: "Reference"
---

The classes, attributes, and `wrapped:` keys that control wrapping. Each
name links to the page that gives its full rules.

## Classes and attributes

These go on a figure, an image, or a table float. On a code cell, the
class goes in `#| classes:`. A code cell figure's width goes in
`#| out-width:` (see
[Get started](get-started.qmd#a-figure-from-a-code-cell)), and a code
cell table takes the document defaults. "All four formats" means HTML, PDF through LaTeX, PDF through Typst, and
Word. HTML includes revealjs slides and dashboards. A table float wraps
in all four formats, except a table that an R package writes as raw
LaTeX or raw Word XML (see [Get started](get-started.qmd#wrap-a-table)).

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Works in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`.wrap-right`](get-started.qmd#wrap-a-figure) | class | none | none | All four formats |
| [`.wrap-left`](get-started.qmd#wrap-a-figure) | class | none | none | All four formats |
| [`.wrap-clear`](stopping.qmd#stop-wrapping-earlier) | class on an empty div | none | none | All four formats |
| [`width`](width-gap.qmd#width) | attribute | A percent of the text column, or a length such as `3in`, `250px`, or `20em`. Each format takes its own set of units. In HTML, also a `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, or `clamp()` value. | The document default, else `40%` | All four formats, each with its own units |
| [`wrap-gap`](width-gap.qmd#gap) | attribute | A length or a percent of the text column. In HTML, also a `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, or `clamp()` value. | The document default, else `1em` | All four formats, each with its own units |
| [`wrap-lines`](formats/latex.qmd#lines-beside-the-figure) | attribute | A number of lines | Counted from the figure's height | PDF through LaTeX only |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18,16,36,15,15]"}

`width` and `wrap-gap` convert to each format's units as the pages for [LaTeX](formats/latex.qmd#width-and-gap),
[Typst](formats/typst.qmd#width-and-gap), and
[Word](formats/word.qmd#width-and-gap) state.

## Document keys

These go under the `wrapped` key in the YAML header of a document or a
project. A figure's own `width` or `wrap-gap` attribute comes first.

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Works in |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`width`](defaults.qmd#rules-for-the-keys) | `wrapped:` key | As the `width` attribute | `40%` | All four formats |
| [`gap`](defaults.qmd#rules-for-the-keys) | `wrapped:` key | As the `wrap-gap` attribute | `1em` | All four formats |
| [`breakpoint`](defaults.qmd#breakpoint) | `wrapped:` key | A length, or a `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, or `clamp()` value with no percent and no `var()` | `576px` | HTML only |

: {tbl-colwidths="[18,16,36,15,15]"}

```yaml
wrapped:
  width: 25%
  gap: 30px
  breakpoint: 800px
```
